extracted.intended_audience: winery proprietors and petitioners seeking viticultural area designation; ATF/regulatory staff (also parole commission staff and prison administrators for the parole rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for petitioning to establish an American Viticultural Area (AVA) (27 CFR part 9) including the kinds of evidence and boundary/map specification required; the page also contains separate final-rule criteria for scheduling parole interim hearings under the Youth Corrections Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of American viticultural area
rubrics_metrics.description: An American viticultural area is defined as a delimited grape growing region distinguishable by geographical features, the boundaries of which must be delineated in subpart C of part 9 (27 CFR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 27 CFR (section cited as 4.25a(e)(1) in the text), an AVA must be a delimited grape‑growing region and distinguishable by geographic features; boundaries must be delineated in subpart C. The rule frames the designation as geographic/distinctness-based, not a quality endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may petition and petitioning procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may petition ATF to establish a grape-growing region as a viticultural area; petitions lead to notice of proposed rulemaking and a public comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure illustrated by the Arroyo Grande Valley petition: proprietors of wineries filed the petition; ATF published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (example: Notice No. 687) with a 45‑day comment period; absence of comments is reported; a final rule specifies effective date. Petitions should include evidence to support distinctness (see climate/soil/boundary/map requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate distinguishable geographic/climatological features (climate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The viticultural area must be shown to be distinguishable from surrounding areas by climatic characteristics (e.g., heat summation region, marine influence, fog patterns, prevailing winds, growing season temperatures, precipitation, elevation and orientation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text provides detailed climate characteristics used to establish Arroyo Grande Valley's distinctness: classification as Region I to II (UC heat summation), marine air influence with morning/evening fog delaying early season growth, moderated onshore flow due to shielding mountains, long dry moderate summers and mild winters, average rainfall (~20 inches with ~80% between Dec–Mar), elevation ranges (sea level to 1,000 ft), summer daytime highs and cool summer nights, orientation (NE–SW) producing prevailing southwesterly winds, and differences in degree‑day totals relative to adjacent AVAs. Expert statements (farm advisor, viticulture professor) corroborating climatic distinctness are shown as supporting evidence. Use of such empirical climate descriptors and expert testimony is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate distinguishable soil characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Soil types and profiles within the proposed AVA should be described to show they differ meaningfully from surrounding areas (e.g., depth, drainage, slope, texture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arroyo Grande Valley example: soils are generally shallow to moderately deep, moderately sloping to extremely steep, well drained; valley floor soils may be very deep, nearly level to moderately sloping, somewhat poorly drained silty clay loam and sandy clay loam. Soil descriptions should indicate how they contribute to viticultural distinctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify and cite approved maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Boundaries must be determinable by reference to specified U.S.G.S. topographical maps (scale and edition identified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule lists the specific 1:24,000 scale USGS maps and editions to be used to determine the Arroyo Grande Valley boundary: 'Arroyo Grande, NE, California' (1965, photorevised 1978), 'Tar Spring Ridge, California' (1967), 'Nipomo, California' (1965), and 'Oceano, California' (1965, photorevised 1979). Petitions should specify appropriate topo maps (scale and edition) so boundaries are unambiguous on official mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary description and metes‑and‑bounds requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The AVA boundary must be described precisely, using roads, peaks, elevations, straight-line bearings, map features, highways, streams and other identifiable landmarks so that the area is unambiguously delimited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register provides a detailed example metes‑and‑bounds description for Arroyo Grande Valley: beginning point intersections of State Routes and local roads, mileages and directions along roads, straight-line mileages to named/unamed peaks with elevations, following proposed road alignments, meanders of unimproved roads, following streams and highways, and returning to the point of beginning. Filings should give exact map-based instructions to allow regulatory staff and the public to locate the boundary on the cited USGS maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated viticultural use within area
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of current viticultural use (vineyards, bonded wineries, acreage planted) within the proposed area supports the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arroyo Grande Valley example cites 'four vineyards totaling 350 acres planted in wine grapes and three bonded wineries.' Including acreage, number of vineyards/wineries and their locations strengthens a petition by showing existing commercial viticulture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling/appellation of origin use and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Once established, the viticultural area name may be used as an appellation of origin in wine labeling and advertising; however, approval does not imply endorsement of wine quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATF explicitly states that approving an AVA allows producers to claim origin distinctions on labels/ads but does not approve or endorse the quality of wines from the area. Any commercial advantage depends on consumer acceptance. Petitions/labels should avoid implying government quality endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and procedural documentation (notice, comment, effective date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment follows notice-and-comment procedures; ATF publishes proposed rule, accepts comments for a defined period, then issues a final rule with an effective date and provides contact information for further inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: notice published July 20, 1989 with a 45‑day comment period ending Sept 5, 1989; no comments received; final rule with effective date Feb 5, 1990. Petitions should anticipate and respond to public comments and provide contact/author info for the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim hearing schedule for Youth Corrections Act (YCA) prisoners – sentence < 7 years
rubrics_metrics.description: For prisoners sentenced under the repealed Youth Corrections Act with sentences of less than seven years, an interim hearing must be scheduled every nine months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule implements a court order (Watts v. Belaski) authorizing 9‑month intervals for YCA prisoners with sentences under 7 years. The regulation revised § 2.65(c)(2) to require scheduling at this interval. The Commission may rely on the court order in setting hearing dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim hearing schedule for Youth Corrections Act (YCA) prisoners – sentence ≥ 7 years
rubrics_metrics.description: For YCA prisoners sentenced to seven years or more, an interim hearing must be scheduled every twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The district court order permits 12‑month intervals for those sentenced to seven years or more; § 2.65(c)(2) was amended accordingly. Rules apply to hearings conducted on or after the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: no further hearings when continued to expiration with < 12 months remaining
rubrics_metrics.description: If a YCA prisoner has been continued to the expiration of his sentence and has less than twelve months remaining before release or transfer to a community treatment center, no further interim hearing is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception (included in § 2.65(c)(2)) was authorized by the court order and incorporated into the regulation to avoid scheduling hearings with little practical effect close to release/transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special interim hearing on receipt of a warden's recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of receipt of any special progress report from the warden recommending parole, a special interim hearing shall be scheduled unless the recommendation can be timely considered at a regularly scheduled interim hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires scheduling such a special hearing promptly, and mandates that an institutional staff member with personal knowledge of the case be present to assist the examiners in evaluating the prisoner's conduct, program performance, and response to treatment. This ensures timely consideration of parole recommendations and informs examiner deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim hearing timing for prisoners with a presumptive parole date close to eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prisoner was granted a presumptive parole date not more than six months beyond the parole eligibility date, and at least 24 months have elapsed since the initial hearing, the prisoner is entitled to an interim hearing six months preceding the month of parole eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment to § 2.14(a)(1)(ii) addresses cases where holding the interim hearing only one month prior to parole eligibility would not allow time for advancement of presumptive date and pre‑release halfway house placement. The rule aims to ensure there is sufficient lead time for procedural steps (advancement for 'superior program achievement', halfway house placement) if the Commission grants an earlier release date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim hearing periodicity for prisoners with maximum term(s) of seven years or more (statutory baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a baseline, prisoners with a maximum term or terms of seven years or more are entitled to interim proceedings every twenty‑four months (until released), subject to the special six‑month‑prior exception described above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 2.14(a)(1)(ii) provides the 24‑month baseline periodicity. However, when the Commission has set a presumptive parole date not more than six months beyond the minimum term and 24 months have elapsed since the initial hearing, the earlier 6‑month pre‑eligibility interim hearing rule applies to permit timely advancement and pre‑release planning.
